summary.headline: Knack Packaging Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 40.5% YoY to INR2,647.7 million, with EBITDA up 53.1% and margin at 22.35%.
summary.overview:
Knack Packaging reported Q1 FY27 as its first earnings call after listing on NSE and BSE. Consolidated revenue grew 40.5% YoY on 20.9% higher volume (10,940 MT), with EBITDA up 53.1% and PAT up 47.96%. Management attributed margin gains to operating leverage, cost discipline, solar power and a rising share of pinch-bottom bags. Capacity utilisation is about 91%, with a rented plant added to bridge until the IPO-funded plant, targeted for October 2027, takes installed capacity to about 70,000 MT.</overview>

segments.name: Domestic vs export
segments.commentary: Management said about 55-56% of sales are export and about 45% domestic; export margins are about 5-6% gross profit higher than domestic. Operations span 74 countries, up from 71 in FY26.

segments.name: PLWPP and pinch-bottom bags
segments.commentary: Pinch-bottom share of sales rose from 19-20% in prior-year quarters to a current 22.5-23%. Management says about 70% of sales are PLWPP bags. Two pinch-bottom machines (about INR20 crore each) were installed in the last quarter of FY26.

guidance_outlook: New IPO-funded plant targeted for commissioning in October 2027, taking installed capacity to about 70,000 MT from about 43,300 MT at listing.
Management expects Q1 FY27 sales levels to be maintained until the new plant starts, using the rented facilities.
Another rented plant of about 5,040 MT annual capacity was added about a month before the call; trials are under way.
Main construction of the new plant is expected to pick up after the monsoon; machinery finalisation is ongoing.
No explicit FY27 volume or EBITDA per kg guidance was given.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 43,300 MT at listing; operating above 48,000 MT including rented facilities, at about 91% utilisation.
Target installed capacity about 70,000 MT once the new plant is commissioned (October 2027).
Management said it is running at 90-92% utilisation and has no spare space to expand existing sites.
11 MW solar farm at Khedbrahma started in the last quarter; electricity cost fell about 1.1% of revenue YoY from solar.
Gross block rose to INR416 crore, with INR141 crore added over the year; the IPO proceeds are about INR320 crore.
demand_pricing: Order book of about INR130 crore cited by management.
Customer retention is about 90%; more than 2,000 customers and over 13,000 SKUs.
Cargill is about 12-17% of revenue (figures varied on the call), with about 600 SKUs and a contract of 2 years plus a 1-year extension, priced as polymer cost plus conversion.
About 45-50% of customers are on fixed conversion-cost pricing with raw material pass-through; the rest are small buyers with pass-through pricing on the day of change.
Management said it passes polymer price changes through to customers on the same day, and that about 50% of input cost changes are passed on, with about 60% retained in some cases.

Management claims about 10% market share in the Indian bag segment (per a Technopack report), and says it is the leader in pinch-bottom bags in India. Management named Polytex (USA) as its only direct listed peer.

qa_highlights.question: Why are ROCE and asset turnover so high versus peers, and how is margin sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said asset turn is 2.53x on gross block and 4.12x on net block as of 30 June 2026, versus peer averages of about 1.5-2x. It attributed this to specialised machinery and a shift to higher-margin pinch-bottom bags. ROCE is supported by ongoing profits and IPO proceeds.

qa_highlights.question: How is the polymer price rise being managed, and how fast is it passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has a SAP S/4HANA forecasting system, buys in cash and in bulk, and passes price changes to customers the same day. It said conversion-cost contracts cover 45-50% of customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Cargill relationship and the FX gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Cargill (USA) business grew from INR4 crore in 2020 to about INR140 crore; it is on a 2+1-year contract and buys finished bags. Management cited the cost of packaging below 1% of product value. FX gain in Q1 FY27 was INR1.6 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How does EBITDA per kg look, and how fast will pinch-bottom volumes move?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited EBITDA per kg of about INR54 in Q1 and INR45 in FY26. Pinch-bottom share is 22.5-23% and is rising; the call did not give a 70,000 MT utilisation timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth be sustained in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q1 sales levels to hold as the rented plants run until the new plant starts in October 2027. It said the onboarding process for new products is long, so marketing is being increased through rented capacity.

risks_watch: Polymer and crude volatility; management said the situation is fully volatile, and pass-through on fixed-conversion contracts shifts cost to the company.
Commissioning timing of the October 2027 plant; construction main phase is after the monsoon.
Dependence on rented plants for interim capacity and on rented facilities until the new plant starts.
Customer concentration: Cargill is about 12-17% of revenue, and figures on the call were inconsistent.
Several figures and facts on the call were inconsistent or corrected (ROCE corrected from 57.73% to 54.73%; Cargill share stated as 12%, 16-17%); verify in filings.
Export share of about 55% and FX exposure; the company reported only INR1.6 crore FX gain in the quarter.
Gross block growth to INR416 crore; management did not commit to maintaining asset turn of 2.5x+ on INR380 crore expansion.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, margins and customer relationships, with a strong emphasis on the 30-year history and first-mover position. Less precise on peer benchmarking, competitor data and volume guidance, where answers were loose and some figures were corrected during the call.
